Question B-007-008-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Scatter is inefficient because only a small fraction of the transmitted energy is redirected toward the skip-zone receiver.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Propagation through ground waves absorbs most of the signal energy": Propagation through ground waves absorbs most of the signal energy uses the wrong path; scatter signals are weak because little energy is scattered usefully.
- sourceIndex 2: "The F region of the ionosphere absorbs most of the signal energy": The F region of the ionosphere absorbs most of the signal energy is not the usual reason; F-region refraction is generally useful rather than strongly absorptive.
- sourceIndex 3: "Auroral activity absorbs most of the signal energy": Auroral activity absorbs most of the signal energy describes a different phenomenon and is not the ordinary HF scatter weakness.
